messages.content: Resuelve problemas de palabras paso a paso.
El tren A sale de la ciudad X a 60 km/h hacia el este. El tren B sale de la ciudad Y (300 km al este) a 80 km/h hacia el oeste, 30 minutos después. ¿Cuándo y dónde se encuentran?

message.content:
The problem is in Spanish: "El tren A sale de la ciudad X a 60 km/h hacia el este. El tren B sale de la ciudad Y (300 km al este) a 80 km/h hacia el oeste, 30 minutos después. ¿Cuándo y dónde se encuentran?" So we have two trains: Train A leaves city X at 60 km/h heading east. Train B leaves city Y (which is 300 km east of X) at 80 km/h heading west, 30 minutes after Train A. We need to find when and where they meet.

We can set up coordinate system: Let X be at position x=0. Then Y is at x=300 km. Train A moves east (positive direction) at 60 km/h starting at t=0 (t measured in hours). Train B moves west (negative direction) at 80 km/h starting at t = 0.5 h (30 min) from x=300 km.

We need to find t_meet > 0.5 h such that positions are equal.

Position of A: x_A(t) = 60 * t.

Position of B: x_B(t) = 300 - 80 * (t - 0.5) for t >= 0.5; for t < 0.5, B hasn't left yet, but we only consider t >= 0.5 because meeting cannot happen before B leaves.

Set x_A(t) = x_B(t) => 60 t = 300 - 80 (t - 0.5) => 60 t = 300 - 80 t + 40 => 60 t + 80 t = 300 + 40 => 140 t = 340 => t = 340 / 140 = 34/14 = 17/7 ≈ 2.428571... hours.

Thus meeting occurs at t ≈ 2.4286 hours after Train A's departure. That's 2 hours + 0.4286*60 = 2 hours + 25.714 minutes ≈ 2 hours 25 minutes 42.86 seconds.
